work_order.understanding: Issue #21 batches 8 non-blocking review findings from PR #20 (for #6). I read each cited line on main: 7 still reproduce, 1 does not. The no-change-edit finding claims updateExpense returns EXPENSE_UPDATED for both kinds, but lib/expenses/actions.ts:400-408 already returns a distinct state ('Nothing to change.') with a distinct EXPENSE_UNCHANGED notice value, covered by lib/expenses/validation.test.ts:496-497 and lib/expenses/actions.test.ts:868 -- a later round fixed it, so it is dropped from this plan per the issue's own instruction and its behavior is kept only as a regression criterion. The live 7: (1) lib/money/format.ts formatBasisPoints exists, is used by percentPartsMessage (lib/expenses/validation.ts:140), and has no direct test file; (2) components/expense-editor.tsx:108 duplicates lib/money/splits.ts parseSplitValue dispatch exactly while the boundary (validation.ts:464,512) already uses the shared helper; (3) style constants + StateMessage/FieldError are byte-identical across expense-editor.tsx, groups-panels.tsx, auth-form.tsx and app/groups/[id]/page.tsx; (4) ConfirmStep is module-private in groups-panels.tsx while DeleteExpenseForm hand-rolls the same shape; (5) the new-expense and edit-expense pages share wrapper/header/banner/Back-link shell; (6) the floorDivide comment (splits.ts:152-156) claims the numerator passes 2^53, but the percentage max is 2147483647x10000=2.1e13 (exact in a double) -- BigInt is genuinely needed only because the shares numerator is total x summed shares, which exceeds 2^53 with a handful of large share counts; (7) splits.test.ts:262-283 sweeps nine fixed totals with no generative input, while TR-4 is proved by property tests over generated splits.
work_order.approach: One behavior-preserving cleanup slice: add a shared presentational module (components/ui.tsx) holding the five byte-identical class constants plus generic StateMessage, FieldError and the existing ConfirmStep, and import it in all four current declaration sites; replace the editor's local parseValue with the already-tested parseSplitValue (identical dispatch, boundary already uses it) and render ConfirmStep inside DeleteExpenseForm with identical copy; extract the new/edit expense shell into components/expense-screen.tsx with a mode prop driving the two archived-banner sentences, and thin both pages to it; correct the floorDivide comment to the true bounds (comment-only, BigInt stays); add a seeded-PRNG generative sweep to splits.test.ts asserting sum preservation and remainder placement; add lib/money/format.test.ts covering formatBasisPoints (the scope finding needs tests, not source changes). No validation, auth, transaction or money-math behavior changes.

No code change.

issue_snapshot.title: Follow-ups from #6: 8 from the review
issue_snapshot.body:
What the review and QA of PR #20 (for #6) found and did not fix there — filed as it merged, one ticket for the lot.

## From the review

Non-blocking findings the reviewer approved despite: a statement about severity, not a judgement that they are wrong.

### Scope: lib/money/format.ts (new formatBasisPoints helper) is in the PR but in neither work-order.json files[] nor tests[].

> Scope: lib/money/format.ts (new formatBasisPoints helper) is in the PR but in neither work-order.json files[] nor tests[].
> 
> `lib/money/format.ts:15`
> 
> Evidence: gh pr diff 20 --name-only lists 14 files including lib/money/format.ts; work-order.json files[] names 10 source paths and tests[] names 3 test paths, none of them lib/money/format.ts.
> 
> Fix: Record it as in-scope support for AC-2's percentage shortfall sentence; no code change needed.

### Reinvention: the editor's local parseValue re-implements lib/money/splits.ts parseSplitValue with identical dispatch.

> Reinvention: the editor's local parseValue re-implements lib/money/splits.ts parseSplitValue with identical dispatch.
> 
> `components/expense-editor.tsx:108`
> 
> Evidence: Editor lines 108-113 dispatch exact->parseMinorUnits, percentage->parseBasisPoints, shares->parseShares, else null; splits.ts parseSplitValue does exactly the same.
> 
> Fix: Import parseSplitValue from ../lib/money/splits and delete the local parseValue.

### A no-change edit tells the user 'Expense updated.' although nothing was written.

> A no-change edit tells the user 'Expense updated.' although nothing was written.
> 
> `lib/expenses/actions.ts:400`
> 
> Evidence: updateExpense returns redirectTo expenseNoticePath(..., EXPENSE_UPDATED) for both the 'updated' and 'unchanged' kinds (actions.ts:400-402); expenseNoticeText maps EXPENSE_UPDATED to 'Expense updated.', so the group page shows that for a no-op save while the 'Nothing to change.' state is discarded by the redirect.
> 
> Fix: When unchanged, return the success state with no redirectTo (the form is still on screen to show it), or add a distinct notice value for it.

### Style constants are copy-pasted into a fourth module instead of shared: expense-editor.tsx re-declares INPUT_CLASSES, PRIMARY_BUTTON, QUIET_BUTTON and DANGER_BUTTON string-identical to groups-panels.tsx and auth-form.tsx, and the group page adds yet another INPUT_CLASSES/QUIET_BUTTON pair.

> Style constants are copy-pasted into a fourth module instead of shared: expense-editor.tsx re-declares INPUT_CLASSES, PRIMARY_BUTTON, QUIET_BUTTON and DANGER_BUTTON string-identical to groups-panels.tsx and auth-form.tsx, and the group page adds yet another INPUT_CLASSES/QUIET_BUTTON pair.
> 
> `components/expense-editor.tsx:51`
> 
> Evidence: gh pr diff 20: expense-editor.tsx:51-57 declares INPUT_CLASSES and QUIET_BUTTON byte-identical to components/groups-panels.tsx:41-47 and components/auth-form.tsx:31-32 on main; app/groups/[id]/page.tsx adds the same two constants again. StateMessage/FieldError likewise redefined per-module (editor:63,77 vs groups-panels:49,63).
> 
> Fix: Export the existing constants from a shared component module and import them in all four places.

### DeleteExpenseForm hand-rolls its own two-step confirm instead of reusing the existing ConfirmStep that groups-panels.tsx documents as the one every destructive action shares.

> DeleteExpenseForm hand-rolls its own two-step confirm instead of reusing the existing ConfirmStep that groups-panels.tsx documents as the one every destructive action shares.
> 
> `components/expense-editor.tsx:535`
> 
> Evidence: components/groups-panels.tsx on main defines module-private ConfirmStep ('a question naming the object, then a pair'), used by ArchiveGroupForm; components/expense-editor.tsx:535-580 re-implements the same shape because the shared one cannot be imported.
> 
> Fix: Export ConfirmStep from groups-panels.tsx and render it inside DeleteExpenseForm.

### The new-expense and edit-expense pages duplicate the same screen shell: identical main wrapper, header block, archived banner (differing only in copy) and Back link.

> The new-expense and edit-expense pages duplicate the same screen shell: identical main wrapper, header block, archived banner (differing only in copy) and Back link.
> 
> `app/groups/[id]/expenses/[expenseId]/edit/page.tsx:62`
> 
> Evidence: gh pr diff 20: edit/page.tsx:62-99 vs new/page.tsx:51-81 — same main wrapper, header shape, archived role=status banner, Back link; only h1 copy, archived sentence and the edit page's delete section differ.
> 
> Fix: One shared expense-screen component taking expenseId: string | null, with a mode prop for the copy differences.

### The floorDivide comment states a false numeric justification: at the top of the admitted amount range total x basis points does not pass the point where a double stops counting one at a time.

> The floorDivide comment states a false numeric justification: at the top of the admitted amount range total x basis points does not pass the point where a double stops counting one at a time.
> 
> `lib/money/splits.ts:153`
> 
> Evidence: lib/money/splits.ts:153-155. Max admitted product is 2147483647 x 10000 = 2.1e13 (percentage) and 2147483647 x 999999 = 2.1e15 (shares), both below 2^53 ~= 9.0e15.
> 
> Fix: Correct the comment or simplify to Math.floor with the bound documented.

### The splits suite proves sum preservation and remainder placement over nine fixed totals, not over generated splits as TR-4 (and AC-4 wording) describes.

> The splits suite proves sum preservation and remainder placement over nine fixed totals, not over generated splits as TR-4 (and AC-4 wording) describes.
> 
> `lib/money/splits.test.ts:264`
> 
> Evidence: lib/money/splits.test.ts:264 loops const totals = [1, 2, 3, 7, 100, 999, 1000, 12345, 2147483] deterministically; no generative input in the file.
> 
> Fix: Randomize the sweep with a seeded PRNG, or soften the TR-4/AC-4 wording to fixed-case coverage.

---

**Check each one still reproduces before planning it.** They were written against the PR as it stood, and a later round can have fixed one. Some may not hold up: say so and drop them rather than implementing something that was never wrong. Split this if they turn out to be unrelated.

Depends on #6.
